disclaimer: This data is compiled from authoritative public sources for informational/educational purposes only. It does not constitute medical advice. Consult qualified healthcare professionals for medical decisions. Ayurvedic entries are literature-sourced and pending expert review — NOT verified medical recommendations.

data.mechanismOfAction: Decreases hepatic glucose production (gluconeogenesis), decreases intestinal absorption of glucose, and improves insulin sensitivity by increasing peripheral glucose uptake and utilization.
data.standardDosage: 500 mg to 1000 mg twice daily with meals (max 2550 mg/day)

howToTake.instructions: Take with meals to minimize stomach upset and gastrointestinal distress. Swallow extended-release tablets whole; do not crush or chew.
howToTake.missedDoseAdvice: Take as soon as remembered with food. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose. Never double up doses.

moderate: Decreased vitamin B12 levels (after long-term use)
urgent: Lactic Acidosis (rare but life-threatening): Extreme weakness, unexplained muscle pain, severe trouble breathing, unusual coldness, slow or irregular heartbeat
Severe allergic reaction (hives, facial or throat swelling)

warnings.blackBox: Risk of Lactic Acidosis, especially in patients with severe renal impairment, sepsis, or acute congestive heart failure.
warnings.alcoholWarning: Avoid excessive alcohol consumption; alcohol potentiates the effect of metformin on lactate metabolism and increases lactic acidosis risk.
foodWarnings: Ensure adequate hydration during hot weather or illness
warnings.pregnancyCaution: Commonly considered safe under specialist endocrinologist supervision; monitor blood glucose closely.

knownInteractions.effect: Acute renal failure and severe lactic acidosis accumulation
knownInteractions.recommendation: Withhold metformin prior to or at time of iodinated contrast procedure, and withhold for 48 hours post-procedure until renal function is confirmed normal.

knownInteractions.effect: Increases metformin blood concentrations while decreasing furosemide concentrations
knownInteractions.recommendation: Monitor blood glucose closely; dosage adjustment may be needed.

knownInteractions.effect: Inhibits renal tubular clearance of metformin, increasing toxicity risk
knownInteractions.recommendation: Consider alternative H2 blockers like famotidine.

data.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits the enzyme converting angiotensin I to angiotensin II, a potent vasoconstrictor. Decreases systemic vascular resistance, reduces blood pressure, and lowers cardiac workload while preserving renal blood flow in diabetic nephropathy.

howToTake.instructions: Can be taken with or without food at the same time each day. Drink plenty of water unless on fluid restrictions.
howToTake.missedDoseAdvice: Take as soon as remembered. If close to next dose, skip and resume regular schedule. Do not take two doses at once.

urgent: Angioedema (life-threatening swelling of lips, tongue, throat, or airway)
Severe dizziness, fainting, or loss of consciousness
Sudden decrease in urination or signs of acute kidney failure

warnings.blackBox: Fetal Toxicity: When pregnancy is detected, discontinue Lisinopril immediately. Can cause fetal harm and death during 2nd and 3rd trimesters.
warnings.alcoholWarning: Alcohol can increase blood-pressure lowering effects, leading to pronounced dizziness or fainting.
foodWarnings: Avoid potassium-based salt substitutes without consulting your physician
Do not take high-dose potassium supplements
warnings.pregnancyCaution: Contraindicated in pregnancy due to severe risk of fetal oligohydramnios and skull hypoplasia.

knownInteractions.effect: Risk of life-threatening hyperkalemia
knownInteractions.recommendation: Monitor serum potassium closely; avoid combination if possible.

knownInteractions.effect: Reduced antihypertensive effect; risk of renal impairment
knownInteractions.recommendation: Monitor blood pressure and renal function; use shortest duration possible.

knownInteractions.effect: Increased lithium levels and toxicity risk
knownInteractions.recommendation: Avoid combination; if necessary, monitor lithium levels frequently.

data.mechanismOfAction: Competitively inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme in cholesterol biosynthesis, reducing hepatic cholesterol synthesis and upregulating LDL receptors, leading to increased LDL clearance.

howToTake.instructions: Take once daily at the same time, with or without food. Evening dosing may be slightly more effective for cholesterol synthesis.
howToTake.bestTimeOfDay: Evening preferred, but consistency matters more
howToTake.missedDoseAdvice: Take as soon as remembered. If close to next dose, skip and resume regular schedule.

urgent: Rhabdomyolysis (rare but life-threatening): Severe muscle pain, dark urine, weakness, fever
Severe liver injury: Jaundice, dark urine, persistent nausea, right upper quadrant pain

warnings.alcoholWarning: Limit alcohol intake; excessive alcohol increases risk of liver injury.
foodWarnings: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice (increases statin levels)
Limit high-fat meals for optimal effect
warnings.pregnancyCaution: Contraindicated in pregnancy (X category); discontinue if pregnancy occurs.

knownInteractions.effect: Markedly increased risk of rhabdomyolysis
knownInteractions.recommendation: Avoid combination; use fenofibrate if fibrate needed.

knownInteractions.effect: Increased atorvastatin exposure and myopathy risk
knownInteractions.recommendation: Limit atorvastatin to 10 mg/day; monitor closely.

knownInteractions.effect: CYP3A4 inhibition increases statin levels
knownInteractions.recommendation: Consider temporary statin hold or dose reduction; monitor for muscle symptoms.

data.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs), leading to cell lysis and death. Active against many Gram-positive and some Gram-negative organisms.
data.standardDosage: 500 mg every 8 hours or 875 mg every 12 hours (adults); pediatric dosing weight-based

howToTake.instructions: Take with or without food. If stomach upset occurs, take with food. Complete the full prescribed course even if symptoms improve.
howToTake.missedDoseAdvice: Take as soon as remembered. If close to next dose, skip and resume regular schedule.

urgent: Severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis): Hives, swelling, difficulty breathing, dizziness
Severe skin reaction (Stevens-Johnson): Blistering, peeling, fever

warnings.alcoholWarning: Alcohol does not directly interact but may worsen side effects like stomach upset.
warnings.pregnancyCaution: Generally considered safe (Category B); widely used in pregnancy when indicated.

knownInteractions.effect: Decreased renal clearance of methotrexate, increasing toxicity
knownInteractions.recommendation: Avoid concurrent use; monitor methotrexate levels if unavoidable.

knownInteractions.effect: Theoretical reduction in contraceptive efficacy
knownInteractions.recommendation: Use backup contraception during treatment and for 7 days after.

knownInteractions.effect: May increase INR and bleeding risk
knownInteractions.recommendation: Monitor INR closely during and after antibiotic course.

data.mechanismOfAction: Central COX inhibition (weak peripheral COX inhibition); reduces prostaglandin synthesis in CNS, raising pain threshold and acting on hypothalamic heat-regulating center for antipyresis.
data.standardDosage: 500-1000 mg every 4-6 hours (max 4000 mg/day adults); pediatric 10-15 mg/kg/dose

howToTake.instructions: Take with or without food. Do not exceed maximum daily dose. Check other medications for paracetamol content to avoid accidental overdose.
howToTake.missedDoseAdvice: Take as soon as remembered if needed. Do not double dose.

urgent: Hepatotoxicity (overdose): Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, jaundice, confusion - MEDICAL EMERGENCY
Severe allergic reaction (rare): Swelling, difficulty breathing

warnings.blackBox: Hepatotoxicity Risk: Do not exceed 4 g/day (adults). Chronic alcohol users and those with liver disease are at higher risk even at lower doses.
warnings.alcoholWarning: Chronic alcohol use significantly increases risk of liver damage. Avoid or limit alcohol.
warnings.pregnancyCaution: Generally considered safe at recommended doses throughout pregnancy; first-line for fever/pain in pregnancy.

knownInteractions.effect: Chronic high-dose paracetamol may increase INR
knownInteractions.recommendation: Monitor INR if using paracetamol regularly (>2 g/day for >3 days).

knownInteractions.effect: Enzyme induction may increase hepatotoxic metabolite formation
knownInteractions.recommendation: Use with caution; monitor liver function if chronic use.

knownInteractions.effect: Increased hepatotoxicity risk
knownInteractions.recommendation: Monitor liver function; avoid if possible.

data.mechanismOfAction: Irreversibly inhibits H+/K+-ATPase (proton pump) in gastric parietal cells, blocking final step of acid secretion. Provides prolonged acid suppression.

howToTake.instructions: Take 30-60 minutes before breakfast. Swallow capsule whole; do not crush or chew. For H. pylori, combine with antibiotics as prescribed.
howToTake.missedDoseAdvice: Take as soon as remembered before a meal. If close to next dose, skip.

urgent: Clostridioides difficile infection: Severe watery/bloody diarrhea
Acute interstitial nephritis: Flank pain, fever, rash

warnings.alcoholWarning: Alcohol may worsen GERD symptoms; no direct drug interaction.
foodWarnings: Take before meals for optimal effect
warnings.pregnancyCaution: Generally considered safe (Category C); use if benefits outweigh risks.

knownInteractions.effect: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, reducing clopidogrel activation
knownInteractions.recommendation: Consider pantoprazole or H2 blocker if PPI needed with clopidogrel.

knownInteractions.effect: Reduced methotrexate clearance, increasing toxicity
knownInteractions.recommendation: Avoid PPIs during high-dose methotrexate; monitor levels.

knownInteractions.effect: Increased digoxin absorption (gastric pH effect)
knownInteractions.recommendation: Monitor digoxin levels if initiating/stopping PPI.

data.mechanismOfAction: Selectively blocks beta-1 adrenergic receptors in the heart, reducing heart rate, contractility, and conduction velocity, thereby lowering myocardial oxygen demand and blood pressure.
data.standardDosage: Tartrate: 50-100 mg twice daily; Succinate ER: 25-200 mg once daily

howToTake.instructions: Take with or immediately after meals to enhance absorption. Do not stop abruptly; taper over 1-2 weeks.
howToTake.bestTimeOfDay: Morning and evening (tartrate) or morning (succinate ER)
howToTake.missedDoseAdvice: Take as soon as remembered. If close to next dose, skip. Do not double dose.

warnings.alcoholWarning: Alcohol potentiates hypotensive effect; may cause dizziness/fainting.
warnings.pregnancyCaution: Category C; use if benefits outweigh risks. Neonatal bradycardia/hypoglycemia reported.

knownInteractions.effect: Additive negative chronotropic/ionotropic effects - severe bradycardia, heart block, hypotension
knownInteractions.recommendation: Avoid combination; if needed, monitor ECG and hemodynamics closely.

knownInteractions.effect: Masks tachycardia warning sign of hypoglycemia
knownInteractions.recommendation: Educate patient on other hypoglycemia symptoms (sweating, tremor); monitor glucose.

knownInteractions.effect: May attenuate antihypertensive effect
knownInteractions.recommendation: Monitor blood pressure; adjust dose if needed.

data.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits calcium ion influx through L-type calcium channels in vascular smooth muscle and cardiac muscle, causing vasodilation and reduced peripheral vascular resistance.

howToTake.instructions: Take once daily at the same time, with or without food. Swallow whole.
howToTake.missedDoseAdvice: Take as soon as remembered. If close to next dose, skip.

urgent: Worsening angina or MI (rare, on initiation/rapid titration)

warnings.alcoholWarning: Alcohol may potentiate hypotensive effect and dizziness.
warnings.pregnancyCaution: Category C; use if benefits outweigh risks. Limited human data.

knownInteractions.effect: Amlodipine weakly inhibits CYP3A4, increasing simvastatin exposure
knownInteractions.recommendation: Limit simvastatin to 20 mg/day with amlodipine.

knownInteractions.effect: Increased immunosuppressant levels
knownInteractions.recommendation: Monitor levels; dose adjustment may be needed.

knownInteractions.effect: Additive hypotensive effect
knownInteractions.recommendation: Monitor blood pressure; titrate carefully.

primaryUses: Edema (Heart Failure, Liver Cirrhosis, Renal Disease)
data.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits Na+/Cl- cotransporter in the distal convoluted tubule, increasing sodium, chloride, and water excretion. Reduces plasma volume and vascular resistance.

howToTake.instructions: Take in the morning to avoid nocturia. Take with food if stomach upset occurs.
howToTake.missedDoseAdvice: Take as soon as remembered. If afternoon, skip to avoid nocturia.

urgent: Severe electrolyte imbalance (severe hypokalemia: arrhythmia risk)

warnings.alcoholWarning: Alcohol potentiates hypotensive effect and dizziness.
foodWarnings: Ensure adequate potassium intake (fruits/vegetables) unless restricted
warnings.pregnancyCaution: Category B; generally avoided in pregnancy unless essential (reduces placental perfusion).

knownInteractions.effect: Decreased lithium clearance, leading to toxicity
knownInteractions.recommendation: Avoid combination; if necessary, monitor lithium levels weekly.

knownInteractions.effect: Hypokalemia increases digoxin toxicity risk
knownInteractions.recommendation: Monitor potassium and digoxin levels; supplement potassium if needed.

knownInteractions.effect: Reduced diuretic and antihypertensive effect; risk of renal impairment
knownInteractions.recommendation: Monitor renal function and blood pressure; avoid chronic NSAID use.

data.mechanismOfAction: Non-selective COX-1 and COX-2 inhibition, reducing prostaglandin synthesis, thereby reducing pain, inflammation, and fever.
data.standardDosage: 200-400 mg every 4-6 hours (max 1200 mg/day OTC, 3200 mg/day prescription)

howToTake.instructions: Take with food or milk to reduce GI irritation. Use lowest effective dose for shortest duration.
howToTake.missedDoseAdvice: Take as soon as remembered if needed. Do not double dose.

urgent: GI bleeding: Black/tarry stools, vomiting blood
Renal failure: Decreased urine, swelling, fatigue
Cardiovascular events: Chest pain, shortness of breath, stroke symptoms

warnings.blackBox: Cardiovascular Thrombotic Events: NSAIDs increase risk of serious CV thrombotic events, MI, stroke. GI Risk: Increased risk of serious GI events including bleeding, ulceration, perforation.
warnings.alcoholWarning: Alcohol increases risk of GI bleeding and liver toxicity.
warnings.pregnancyCaution: Avoid in 3rd trimester (premature ductus arteriosus closure). Category C (1st/2nd), D (3rd).

knownInteractions.effect: Additive bleeding risk (antiplatelet + anticoagulant + GI irritation)
knownInteractions.recommendation: Avoid combination; if essential, monitor INR closely and consider PPI.

knownInteractions.effect: Reduced antihypertensive effect; risk of renal impairment
knownInteractions.recommendation: Monitor blood pressure and renal function; avoid chronic use.

knownInteractions.effect: Decreased methotrexate clearance, increasing toxicity
knownInteractions.recommendation: Avoid concurrent use.

data.mechanismOfAction: Binds 50S ribosomal subunit, inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis. Concentrates in tissues with long half-life allowing short-course therapy.
data.standardDosage: 500 mg day 1, then 250 mg daily x 4 days (or 500 mg x 3 days); single 1 g for chlamydia

howToTake.instructions: Take 1 hour before or 2 hours after food. If GI upset, may take with food. Complete full course.
howToTake.missedDoseAdvice: Take as soon as remembered. If close to next dose, skip.

urgent: Torsades de pointes (QT prolongation with risk factors)
Severe hepatotoxicity: Jaundice, dark urine, RUQ pain

warnings.blackBox: QT Prolongation: Risk of torsades de pointes. Avoid in patients with known QT prolongation, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, or on other QT-prolonging drugs.
warnings.alcoholWarning: No direct interaction; alcohol may worsen GI side effects.
foodWarnings: Take on empty stomach for optimal absorption
warnings.pregnancyCaution: Category B; generally considered safe when indicated.

knownInteractions.effect: May increase INR and bleeding risk
knownInteractions.recommendation: Monitor INR during and after azithromycin course.

knownInteractions.effect: Increased digoxin levels (P-gp inhibition)
knownInteractions.recommendation: Monitor digoxin levels.

knownInteractions.effect: Reduced azithromycin absorption
knownInteractions.recommendation: Separate by 2 hours.

data.mechanismOfAction: Selective peripheral H1 receptor antagonist; minimal CNS penetration causing less sedation than first-generation antihistamines.
data.standardDosage: 10 mg once daily (5 mg for mild symptoms); pediatric 2.5-5 mg

howToTake.instructions: Take once daily, with or without food. Can be taken at night if drowsiness occurs.
howToTake.missedDoseAdvice: Take as soon as remembered. If close to next dose, skip.

warnings.alcoholWarning: Alcohol may increase drowsiness; avoid driving/operating machinery if affected.
warnings.pregnancyCaution: Category B; preferred antihistamine in pregnancy if needed.

knownInteractions.effect: Additive sedation
knownInteractions.recommendation: Caution with driving/operating machinery.

knownInteractions.effect: Slightly increased theophylline levels
knownInteractions.recommendation: Monitor if high-dose theophylline.

data.mechanismOfAction: Selective beta-2 adrenergic agonist causing bronchial smooth muscle relaxation, rapid onset (minutes), duration 4-6 hours.
data.standardDosage: 100-200 mcg (1-2 puffs) as needed; max 800 mcg/day; before exercise 15-30 min prior

howToTake.instructions: Shake inhaler well. Exhale fully, place mouthpiece in mouth, actuate while inhaling slowly and deeply. Hold breath 10 sec. Rinse mouth after use.
howToTake.bestTimeOfDay: As needed for symptoms or before trigger exposure
howToTake.missedDoseAdvice: Not applicable (as-needed). If using regularly and missed, take as soon as remembered.

urgent: Paradoxical bronchospasm (worsening wheezing after use) - STOP and seek care

warnings.blackBox: Paradoxical Bronchospasm: Can cause life-threatening bronchospasm. If occurs, discontinue immediately and treat with alternative bronchodilator.
warnings.pregnancyCaution: Category C; use if benefits outweigh risks. Uncontrolled asthma poses greater fetal risk.

knownInteractions.effect: Beta-blockers antagonize beta-2 effect, causing severe bronchospasm
knownInteractions.recommendation: Avoid non-selective beta-blockers in asthma/COPD. Cardioselective beta-1 blockers may be used with caution.

knownInteractions.effect: Additive hypokalemia risk
knownInteractions.recommendation: Monitor potassium with high-dose/frequent salbutamol.

knownInteractions.effect: Potentiated cardiovascular effects
knownInteractions.recommendation: Use with caution; monitor cardiac status.

data.mechanismOfAction: Modified human insulin with prolonged, peakless action profile (~24 hours). Forms microprecipitates at injection site for slow, steady absorption providing basal insulin coverage.
data.standardDosage: Individualized; typically 0.2-0.4 units/kg/day Type 1; 10-20 units/day Type 2 start; titrate to fasting glucose target

howToTake.instructions: Inject subcutaneously once daily at the same time each day. Rotate injection sites (abdomen, thigh, upper arm). Do not mix with other insulins.
howToTake.bestTimeOfDay: Consistent time daily (often bedtime or morning)
howToTake.missedDoseAdvice: If within 2 hours of usual time, take full dose. If >2 hours, check glucose and take partial dose; consult provider.

urgent: Severe hypoglycemia: Confusion, seizures, unconsciousness - GLUCAGON/IV DEXTROSE

warnings.blackBox: Hypoglycemia: Most common adverse effect. Can be life-threatening. Risk increased with missed meals, exercise, alcohol, renal/hepatic impairment. Never share pen/device. Do not mix with other insulins.
warnings.alcoholWarning: Alcohol increases hypoglycemia risk (impairs gluconeogenesis); can cause delayed hypoglycemia. Never drink on empty stomach.
warnings.pregnancyCaution: Category B; insulin requirements change during pregnancy; intensive monitoring required.

knownInteractions.effect: Mask hypoglycemia symptoms (tachycardia, tremor)
knownInteractions.recommendation: Educate patient on neuroglycopenic symptoms; monitor glucose closely.

knownInteractions.effect: Increased risk of fluid retention and heart failure
knownInteractions.recommendation: Monitor for edema/heart failure; consider dose reduction.

knownInteractions.effect: May increase hypoglycemia risk
knownInteractions.recommendation: Monitor glucose; dose adjustment may be needed.

data.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase, reducing synthesis of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors (II, VII, IX, X) and proteins C & S. Requires INR monitoring.
data.standardDosage: Highly individualized; target INR typically 2.0-3.0 (2.5-3.5 for mechanical valves); typical 2-10 mg/day

howToTake.instructions: Take at the same time each day (usually evening). Consistent vitamin K intake (leafy greens). Regular INR monitoring essential. Do not change dose without provider guidance.
howToTake.missedDoseAdvice: If same day, take as soon as remembered. If next day, skip and resume; do not double. Contact provider if >1 dose missed.

urgent: Major bleeding: GI bleed, intracranial hemorrhage, hematuria - MEDICAL EMERGENCY

warnings.blackBox: Bleeding Risk: Major/fatal bleeding can occur. INR monitoring essential. Numerous drug/food interactions. Genetic variability (CYP2C9, VKORC1).
warnings.alcoholWarning: Alcohol increases INR and bleeding risk (liver metabolism); acute intake increases effect, chronic may decrease. Avoid binge drinking.
foodWarnings: Maintain consistent vitamin K intake (leafy greens, broccoli, Brussels sprouts)
warnings.pregnancyCaution: Category X - Contraindicated. Causes fetal hemorrhage, teratogenicity (warfarin embryopathy). Use LMWH in pregnancy.

knownInteractions.effect: Additive bleeding risk (antiplatelet + anticoagulant + GI irritation)
knownInteractions.recommendation: Avoid NSAIDs; use paracetamol for pain. If aspirin indicated (e.g., post-stent), monitor INR closely.

knownInteractions.effect: Reduced vitamin K production by gut flora, increasing INR
knownInteractions.recommendation: Monitor INR 3-5 days after starting/stopping antibiotics.

knownInteractions.effect: Potent CYP2C9 inhibition, dramatically increasing warfarin effect
knownInteractions.recommendation: Reduce warfarin dose 30-50%; monitor INR frequently (twice weekly initially).
